From waste collection to value recovery: building a better pathway.

Packaging may have value beyond the product it carries. But recovering that value depends on what happens after consumption. Littering, improper disposal and gaps in collection systems can prevent packaging waste from entering organised recovery channels, putting its material value at risk.

A Deposit Refund Scheme (DRS) creates a structured return pathway. It links DRS-eligible empty packaging to a nominal refundable deposit, encouraging its return through designated collection channels, and by creating a defined route after consumption it can help capture material that might otherwise be missed by conventional collection systems.

The quality of collection also shapes the potential for recovery. Contamination and poor handling can reduce material quality, affecting how effectively it can be recycled and the value that can ultimately be recovered.

From capturing discarded packaging to preparing it for recycling, every stage contributes to the recovery journey. DRS can strengthen the return and collection stage, while effective sorting, processing and recycling help turn that collected material into a usable resource.

The goal is not simply to collect packaging, but to help its material value find a way back into the economy.

Swipe through the pathway, step by step.
